name: 希尔妲
who: Hilda, a human girl of the far north who has carried fire from hearth to hearth for over twenty thousand years and still has the face of a fifteen-year-old: small, about 152 cm, wholly covered by her clothes. Ash-gold hair in one thick braid hanging below the waist, the end tied with a short piece of faded red yarn, the fringe always tousled by the wind. Bright amber eyes like embers just raked open, looking straight at people. Around her neck on a leather cord hangs a small smoke-blackened clay pot, a ring of white frost around its mouth and one tiny ember glowing deep inside it; the pot is no bigger than her fist and she wears it at her neck in every outfit. A stubborn, plain-spoken, warm air: still a fifteen-year-old's temper, only having seen more.
face: FACE, as in the references: medium-large, sharp, gently slanted almond eyes of bright amber, NOT big round doll eyes; a thin tapering dark-brown upper lash line and a fine eyelid crease; thin eyebrows partly hidden by the tousled fringe; a light scatter of small freckles across the bridge of the nose; cheeks pink-red from the cold all year round; a tiny nose; a small mouth that smiles with the lips closed, ordinary human teeth, NO fangs and NO pointed canines; a youthful, bright face with a neat small chin. Skin shadows are a soft warm pink-orange.
palette: warm ember orange and amber, ash gold, fox russet and snow white, a little faded red
casual: Her travelling clothes: her late father's fox-fur coat, two sizes too big, the sleeves rolled up three times, belted at the waist with a hemp rope, a hood trimmed with fox-tail fur hanging down her back; under it a thick undyed wool tunic to the knees and wool leggings; hide boots wrapped round and round with leather thongs; a pair of mittens on a string around her neck. On her back a tall basket woven of birch bark and willow, a head taller than she is, dry straw sticking out of its top: this basket rim is the only thing allowed to rise above her head. She stands sturdy and cheerful with a closed-mouth smile, one hand on the basket strap.
private: Resting by someone else's fire: the fur coat off, a long-sleeved, high-collared undyed wool dress to the shins with red yarn stitching at the cuffs, thick knitted stockings and the hide boots, the braid hanging over one shoulder. She holds a handful of roasted chestnuts and is peeling one, a sleepy, contented closed-mouth smile.
battle: Ready to hold a line of fire: the fox-fur coat belted tight, the hood down, the mittens tucked into the rope belt, leather bracers over the sleeves, the basket left behind. In her right hand she grips a short wooden torch, a plain stick wrapped at the tip, its small flame lit from her clay pot, held forward at chest height; the one small clay pot stays hanging at her neck on its cord, there is no second pot; her left hand is a fist at her side; a fierce, unafraid look, the brows drawn together, the mouth closed.
formal: At a midwinter fire-lighting rite: a long deep-red wool dress with long sleeves and a high collar, the hem and cuffs embroidered with a band of small white flame shapes, a short white fur capelet with a hood, the braid freshly tied with new red yarn, the clay pot hung on a fine silver chain. She stands very straight with the hands folded in front, a quiet, solemn little smile.
art: A head-and-shoulders portrait, the face turned slightly, the amber eyes looking straight at the viewer with an open, warm, unflinching look, a small closed-mouth grin, no teeth showing. She cups the smoke-blackened clay pot near her chin in both mittened hands, the ember inside warming the underside of her face, while cool snow light comes from one side. Foreground blur: falling snowflakes and a few drifting sparks. She wears the fox-fur coat with the fox-tail hood around her shoulders.
battle_pose: 3) the battle outfit: braced and fierce, the shoulders squared, the feet a little wider and planted, the brows drawn together and the mouth closed, gripping a short wooden torch in one hand close to the body; she is not smiling in this one.

name: 霍布
who: Hob, a human farm boy who became a legend of the harvest and has looked nineteen for over twenty thousand years, still looking like a sleepy youth: about 166 cm, a little short, soft and round-cheeked, a grown young man and not a child. Soft, fluffy wheat-gold hair with a few wheat awns caught in it, a face full of freckles, half-lidded sleepy hazel eyes, cheeks that puff up round when he smiles. Around his neck a cord braided from wheat straw with a single dry grain of wheat threaded on it. A lazy, haggling, good-natured air; he cannot bear to see anyone go hungry.
face: FACE, as in the references: a young man's soft, boyish face, NOT angular: half-lidded, sleepy, gently slanted hazel eyes with a thin tapering dark-brown upper lash line; straight light-brown eyebrows; a sprinkle of freckles across the nose and cheeks; soft rounded cheeks and a small rounded chin; a small nose shown by a faint shadow; a relaxed mouth with a lazy half-smile. Clean skin with very little shading; skin shadows are a soft warm tone.
palette: wheat gold and warm straw, flour white, soft brown homespun, a little leaf green
casual: His everyday clothes: a loose, coarse homespun miller's smock in faded oatmeal, belted with a cord, the sleeves rolled to the elbow, baggy brown linen trousers tucked into worn, patched leather shoes; an empty flour sack slung over one shoulder. He holds a half-eaten heel of bread, a sleepy half-smile.
private: Lazing about at harvest time: an untucked, loose cream linen shirt with the collar open and the sleeves pushed up, braces hanging loose at the hips, rolled-up brown trousers, barefoot. He hugs the folded empty flour sack under one arm like a pillow and yawns, the eyes almost closed.
battle: On the road to a famine: a weathered oilcloth travelling cloak over the smock, a wide straw hat hanging on his back, cloth gaiters wrapped over sturdy boots, a seed pouch and a small harvest sickle hanging at the belt. He never fights and carries no weapon: in place of one he shoulders a heavy, bulging sack of grain, gripping it with both hands, the knees braced, a rare determined look.
battle_pose: 3) the road outfit: braced and determined, the shoulders set, the feet a little wider and planted, a firm expression, carrying the heavy grain sack on one shoulder with both hands; he never fights and holds no weapon.
formal: Guest of honour at the long harvest tables: his one good set, a clean cream linen shirt buttoned to the collar, a brown wool waistcoat with wooden buttons, a wheat-gold sash, a small bunch of wheat ears pinned at the chest, neat brown trousers and polished old shoes, the straw cord with the grain still at his neck. For once he stands up straight, the hands clasped in front, a polite, slightly sleepy smile.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the half-lidded hazel eyes looking at the viewer with a lazy, knowing smile, a stalk of wheat between his teeth. Warm low evening sun from one side lights his fluffy wheat-gold hair and his freckles. Foreground blur: ripe wheat ears, drifting chaff and seeds. He wears the oatmeal miller's smock, the straw cord with the single grain at his throat.

name: 凯恩
who: Kain, a human mountain herdsman who held a whole summer of thunder in his breath and has looked twenty-five ever since: about 182 cm, sturdy, with a broad, deep chest. Black hair singed by lightning into small tight curls, deep storm-grey eyes in which faint lightning flickers, a thin white scar line along the jaw. Fair, clean skin, not tanned. Silver-white lightning-fern patterns branch across his chest and down both arms, the path the lightning took through him. A quiet, slow, low-voiced air, like a thundercloud that has not yet broken.
build: Sturdy and broad-chested, strong without bulk.
palette: storm grey and slate blue, silver-white lightning, tawny leopard gold, dark wool brown
casual: His herdsman's clothes: a knee-length brown wool robe with short sleeves, belted, over dark leggings and laced hide boots, and over it a sleeveless vest of thunder-patterned leopard skin whose markings glow faintly like distant lightning. At his hip his father's ox horn, a wolf's tooth tied to it on a thong. He holds a white-ash herding staff with an iron-capped head, held low at an angle. A calm, unhurried look.
private: At his mountain door: a loose undyed wool shirt, the collar open on the silver fern marks and the sleeves pushed up, plain wool trousers, barefoot. He holds a small lamb in the crook of one arm, a quiet, gentle look.
battle: Ready to call down the storm: the leopard-skin vest over a dark leather jerkin, leather bracers, the ox horn at his hip. He grips the iron-capped white-ash staff in both hands across his body, small arcs of lightning crawling along the silver fern marks on his arms and around the iron cap, his grey eyes lit white; a still, intent look.
formal: Called down to a lowland lord's hall: a long dark slate-grey wool robe to the ankles, silver lightning-fern embroidery climbing the sleeves and collar, the leopard skin worn as a short mantle over one shoulder, the ox horn on a braided cord, the curls tamed a little. He stands upright, the hands loosely clasped in front, a grave and quiet look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the storm-grey eyes looking at the viewer from under the singed black curls with a quiet, heavy calm, the lips closed as if holding a breath. Cold silver-blue storm light from one side; faint lightning traces along the fern marks on his neck and collarbone. Foreground blur: dark rain streaks, drifting grass seeds and a distant flash of lightning. He wears the leopard-skin vest over the brown wool robe.
art_extra: His hair is short, the same small, tight, lightning-singed curls as in the sprite, ending above the collar, not long and not wavy.

name: 珀拉
who: Pora, a human pearl diver of the sunken Pearl Bay who has looked nineteen for twenty thousand years: a young face of nineteen, about 163 cm. Long ink-black hair with a deep blue sheen at the ends, drifting loose as if in slow water. Pale grey eyes with a hint of blue, like pearls, bright when she looks at someone. The pale white skin of someone who lives in the water. Long fingers marked with tiny healed cuts from oyster shells. On her head the Pearl Crown of the old Pearl Bay kings, a circlet set only with pearls that glow a soft pale blue in shadow; at her throat a single uneven pearl on a cord. Her lips are usually pressed shut, holding a year's breath; a stubborn, composed, quiet air.
build: 163 cm, slender and long-limbed: thin but strong shoulders and back, a medium bust, a narrow waist and gently rounded hips.
palette: deep sea blue and teal, pearl white and silver, a soft aqua glow
casual: Her pearl diver's clothes: a white linen short-sleeved tunic wrapped and tied at the waist, falling to mid-thigh over knee-length white linen breeches, a rope belt for a net bag with a small oyster knife hanging from it, bare feet; the glowing pearl crown, the uneven pearl at her throat. She stands with the hands loosely at her sides, the hair drifting, a calm, closed-lipped look.
private: On the shore at the great low tide: a long, loose sea-blue linen dress with long sleeves, a pale knitted shawl around her shoulders, bare feet, the crown set aside and a simple cord of white pearls tying back her hair. She holds the uneven pearl up in her palm, a soft, faraway look.
battle: Singing against the sea: a fitted sea-green diver's wrap over the linen breeches, sea-glass armlets, the rope belt, the pearl crown blazing pale blue. She grips the small oyster knife low in one hand, the other hand at her throat, the lips parted as if about to sing; a fierce, steady look.
formal: At a coastal rite as the bearer of the Pearl Bay crown: a long layered gown of white linen and sheer sea-blue silk with long flowing sleeves, strings of small pearls along the hem and neckline, a pale silver-blue mantle, the pearl crown glowing. She stands very upright, the hands folded in front, a serene, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the pale grey-blue eyes looking at the viewer, the lips pressed shut. She is underwater: soft wavering light from the surface above falls across her shoulders, her ink-black hair spreading in the water in big clean shapes, the pearl crown glowing pale blue. Foreground blur: drifting bubbles, a few glowing pearls and rays of light. She wears the white linen tunic, the uneven pearl at her throat.

name: 卡兰缇娅
who: Calantia, an elf of the old forest's Watcher clan who has kept her watch for some thirteen thousand years: tall, about 174 cm, slim, with very long legs. Skin pale as someone who lives under the canopy. Long pale-green hair shading to silver, in one long braid hanging below the waist. Long pointed elf ears. Amber eyes that gaze at far things without blinking and blink quickly when she looks at people. Two faint wind-reddened streaks across her cheekbones that never faded. A quiet, curious air; the first thing she asks anyone is their name and how to write it.
build: 174 cm, tall and slim with long legs: a small bust, a narrow waist and slim hips.
palette: faded grey-green and moss, pale silver-green, warm amber, antler ivory
casual: Her Watcher's clothes: a long hooded cloak, once grey-green and sun-bleached to grey-white, patched in several places, a few dry leaves stitched along the edge of the hood (the hood down); under it a moss-green tunic, fitted dark leggings and soft knee-high boots, a leather pouch of small carving knives at the belt, and hanging at her hip a short piece of deer antler carved with a single name, her own. She holds a small carving knife and an antler tine she is carving, a curious look.
private: At ease in the forest market: a soft, loose oatmeal linen tunic dress with long sleeves, a knitted moss-green shawl, soft leather leggings and slippers, the braid over one shoulder with a sprig of leaves in it. She turns a half-carved antler in her fingers, a gentle, absorbed look.
battle: On watch at a tower: the patched grey-white cloak pinned back, a leather bracer on the bow arm, a quiver of grey-fletched arrows at the hip, the antler at her belt. She grips her great longbow, a little taller than she is, held diagonally across her body, an arrow nocked and the string not drawn; a still, piercing look.
formal: Before the elven high court: a long silvery-green robe embroidered along the hems with small leaves and antler shapes, a long pale mantle in place of the old cloak, a thin circlet of woven twigs and pale leaves, the carved antler on a silver cord at her waist. She stands tall and still, the hands folded, a calm, solemn look.
art: A portrait with the camera tilted, the face large, the amber eyes looking past the viewer into the distance, unblinking, the long ear and the pale silver-green braid sweeping across the frame. Cool forest light filtering through leaves from one side. Foreground blur: drifting leaves and a carved piece of antler hanging on a cord. She wears the patched grey-white hooded cloak with dry leaves stitched along the hood.
